main_body: palm tree: a drooping frond crown seen from above, on a curved tan trunk
top_band: light green frond crown seen from above, x=15 rows 1-18 (lightest #aedc66 at row 5, #82c240 rows 6-14); the dark outline at row 20 closes it; the trunk is below at the side columns
evidence: The crown is a wide, lighter, foreshortened horizontal mass whose fronds radiate and droop. It sits above and overhangs the tan trunk, and the dark underside of the fronds shades the trunk top. It is not a flat elevation or a thin rim. The trunk is a thin vertical cylinder, which is normal for a plant. The crown reads as a seen-from-above surface over a vertical support, so it is acceptable for an organic object.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 14 distinct colours and 11 per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours for the references. All of its dark edge pixels are neutral near-black (100%, #0e0a0c), which gives a uniform sticker outline, whereas the references' outlines carry a material tint (0% neutral). The frond ramp has about 4-5 green steps and the trunk about 3-4 tans. There are no leaf clumps or per-leaf texture, only smooth bands and a few dots. Next to the clustered, richly shaded reference canopies it looks much thinner and flatter.
